title: All Letters Unique
statement: Given a string word, return true if all letters are unique. Ignore case and ignore non-letter characters.
think: What is the task asking? Check whether any letter repeats.
What is the key operation? Quickly tell whether a letter was seen before.
What wording signals stand out? Unique, duplicate, seen before.
What is the brute force idea? Compare each letter with every other letter.
What is the better/optimal idea? Add letters to a set and fail on duplicates.
What are the edge cases? Mixed case, spaces, punctuation.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(k) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I scan letters and return false as soon as a letter appears twice.
algorithm: If letter already in set -> return false
interview: I would use a HashSet because the only question is whether a letter was seen before.
ru: Это задача вида seen before. Как только буква встретилась второй раз, ответ false.
visualExplanation:
word = "Hello"
h -> add
e -> add
l -> add
l -> already seen -> false

critical: Use Dictionary when only seen/not seen is needed

gaps: Nice to have: explain why HashSet is enough
constraints: Assume the input may contain letters and other characters.
whyThisPattern: This is a HashSet problem because we only need membership checking for previously seen letters.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because counts are unnecessary.
Not Two Pointers, because there is no need to compare from both ends.
